neighbours.label: a digit or word piece that completes a famous fixed identifier (November 11 Armistice, Chicxulub, H1N1, 65 million years)
fire: Fighting on the Western Front stopped at eleven o'clock on November 11, 1918.
Geologists traced the buried Chicxulub structure beneath the Yucatán Peninsula.
In 2009, the swine flu strain known as H1N1 spread rapidly around the world.
Every year on November 11, Britain falls silent to remember the 1918 Armistice.
The asteroid that formed the Chicxulub crater was roughly ten kilometers wide.
Doctors urged pregnant women to get the H1N1 vaccine during the 2009 pandemic.
Non-avian dinosaurs vanished about 66 million years ago at the end of the Cretaceous.
Veterans Day is held on November 11 because the First World War ended on that date.
quiet: Fighting at the county fair stopped at eleven o'clock on November 21, 2018.
Geologists traced the buried limestone layer beneath the farmland near Dayton.
In 2009, the new flu clinic opened on the north side of town.
Every year on November 18, the town holds a lantern parade by the river.
The asteroid that passed Earth last spring was roughly ten meters wide.
Doctors urged pregnant women to get plenty of rest during the hot summer.
The old maple tree was planted about 61 years ago at the edge of the park.
The garage sale is held on April 11 because the weather is usually mild by then.

predictions: The second '1' of the Armistice date, the 'ub' of Chicxulub and the final digit of H1N1 fire; the same tokens in ordinary dates and numbers stay quiet.
